candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — newborn screening, early identification of health problems, and caregiver education about preventive/screening services
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — newborn screening and follow-up
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that newborn screening identifies risk rather than confirming diagnosis and that out-of-range results require timely follow-up testing even when the infant appears well.

options.A: No. Newborn screening identifies babies who may have a condition; an out-of-range result usually requires timely follow-up and often diagnostic testing
options.B: Yes. Newborn screening is diagnostic, so an out-of-range result confirms the condition without additional testing
options.C: No. Out-of-range newborn screening results can be ignored unless the baby develops symptoms
options.D: Yes. Newborn screening is performed only when a baby already has symptoms or a strong family history

candidate.rationale: HRSA explains that newborn screening and diagnostic testing are not the same. Screening checks whether a newborn might have certain serious conditions and is intended to connect affected infants with early care. An out-of-range screen does not by itself establish the diagnosis; timely follow-up, often including diagnostic testing, is needed. Waiting for symptoms can delay treatment for conditions in which early intervention matters. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Newborn screening is not diagnostic; it identifies infants who may have serious conditions and an out-of-range result requires timely follow-up testing.
candidate.source_document_title: About Newborn Screening; Newborn Screening Process
candidate.source_locator: About Newborn Screening > 'Are Screening and Diagnostic Testing the Same?': screening cannot determine whether a baby actually has a condition; out-of-range screens require follow-up, often diagnostic testing. Newborn Screening Process: blood spot, pulse oximetry, and hearing screening identify babies who might have serious conditions and require follow-up when results are out of range
